title: Four Ahead at the Third, Six Behind at the Last: The Baker Brothers in Catalonia
title_candidates: Four Ahead at the Third, Six Behind at the Last: The Baker Brothers in Catalonia
Two Course Records and a Family Argument: Jon Baker Takes TEG 11
The Bridesmaid Gets the Jacket: Jon Baker's Catalonian Double
Brotherly Love, Six Points Wide: TEG 11 in Girona
theme: Two brothers, one trophy: Jon Baker built the gross week of his life while Alex Baker, the defending champion, held a four-shot lead three holes into the final round of the TEG 11 Trophy and then dismantled it hole by hole on the Stadium course — with David Mullin, owner of eight Green Jackets, sliding quietly to the Wooden Spoon behind them.
tone: house — subverted gravitas, British English, restraint and exact numbers; tongue-in-cheek celebration of Jon Baker, forensic sympathy for the collapses
opening_hook: Open on the 3rd green at PGA Catalunya - Stadium in R4, Alex Baker four clear of his brother and the TEG 11 Trophy apparently settled — then rewind, because the next fifteen holes cost him eleven points and the title.

trophy_storyline.subject: How the TEG 11 Trophy changed hands twice between brothers: Jon Baker's 45-hole lead lost at El Prat, then Alex Baker's four-shot final-round lead surrendered in eleven points
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: The main event was decided not by anything Jon Baker did on the Sunday but by his brother's collapse from four clear after three holes to the worst round of his TEG career.
trophy_storyline.shape: Jon Baker led the Trophy from R1 H4 for 45 straight holes, through a 35 at the Stadium and a 41 on the Tour, before a triple-laced stretch at El Prat's 11th to 13th handed the lead outright to Alex Baker at R3 H13 (b01, b23, b42). Alex Baker was four ahead by the 3rd of R4 and then bled seven shots at 4-6, eight at 12-14 and eight more at 16-18, with quadruple bogeys at the 9th (SI 1) and the 17th, for 27 points — his worst round to date (b02, b31, b33, b18, b11, b08, b04). Jon Baker, who dropped four shots himself at the 13th, simply posted 35, drew level at the 6th, and walked in on 143 points, six clear (b06, b05).

trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: Alex Baker's Four-Shot Lead Lasted Three Holes
trophy_storyline.standfirst: Jon Baker had led the Trophy for 45 holes before losing it at El Prat, and needed only an ordinary 35 on the Stadium course to take it back by six as his brother's final round unravelled in three separate collapses.

jacket_storyline.subject: Jon Baker's gross week: two course records in two days, the Jacket lead held after every round, and the end of David Mullin's run of Green Jackets
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Jon Baker had been Jacket runner-up in three of the last four TEGs without a win, and he finally took it off the man with eight of them.
jacket_storyline.shape: Jon Baker opened with 90 gross at PGA Catalunya - Stadium, a new course record beating the previous 94, then 84 on the Tour course, another record beating 89 — nine and six shots better respectively than his own marks from TEG 6 (cr01, cr02). David Mullin, back-to-back Jacket holder going in, got his nose in front at El Prat's 5th after Jon Baker had led the gross for 37 holes, and lost it again at the very next hole (b30). Jon Baker led the Jacket after every round and closed at +70, three clear of Mullin, whose own new personal bests at the Tour (85) and Stadium (91) courses were not enough (b09).

jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: Two Course Records, One Green Jacket
jacket_storyline.standfirst: Jon Baker rewrote the gross records at both PGA Catalunya courses in successive days, and finally converted three near-misses into the Jacket at the expense of David Mullin, the holder of eight.

spoon_storyline.subject: David Mullin takes the TEG 11 Wooden Spoon by ten points while finishing Jacket runner-up with new personal bests at two of the three courses
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The steadiest man in the field, round to round, was steadily last: Mullin never once reached the top half of the Stableford on any of the four days.
spoon_storyline.shape: Mullin sat fourth on points after two rounds despite an 85 at the Tour course and a ten-point burst at its 8th to 10th (b50), then El Prat undid him: a four-over 7 at the par-three 6th and five successive holes without a net par from the 11th dropped him to the bottom of the Spoon race at R3 H12 (b20, b25). He answered with three pars for nine points to open R4 (b27, b34), which flattered nobody once the 15th to 17th cost him seven shots and three blank net holes (b16, b13). Final tally 125 points — ten adrift of John Patterson, the next worst, and the Spoon accepted with the gross runner-up's certificate in the other hand (b39).

spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: Eight Jackets, And Now A Spoon
spoon_storyline.standfirst: David Mullin shot personal bests at both PGA Catalunya courses and came second in the gross, yet finished the Stableford ten points behind anyone else after El Prat's back nine and the Stadium's closing stretch took their cut.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's four rounds of demolition: two nines, an eleven, a course-worst 103, and a Spoon dodged by ten points
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The reigning Wooden Spoon holder produced the single worst hole and the worst round in the field's history at the Tour course and still finished ten points clear of last.
discovered_storylines.shape: Patterson's R1 at the Stadium ran to nines at the 4th and the 13th and eights at the 10th and the 17th, eleven shots gone between the 12th and the 14th, and the bottom of the Spoon race by H14 (b32, b28, b41, b37). R2 brought an eleven at the par-five 15th — six over on one hole — and a 103, a new course-worst at PGA Catalunya - Tour, beating the previous 101 (b10, cr03). Then the rally nobody noticed: nine points from the 8th to the 10th at El Prat despite a nine at the 16th, and a closing R4 in which he bled seven shots at 7-9 and eight more at 12-14 yet still birdied-adjacent his way to pars at the 16th and 17th, closing to eight off the Trophy lead after trailing by sixteen (b38, b07, b24, b26, b14, b17, b22).

discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Patterson's Eleven, And The Spoon Dodged
discovered_storylines.standfirst: John Patterson arrived as the holder of the Wooden Spoon, posted the worst gross round the Tour course has seen and a six-over eleven at its 15th, and somehow handed the trinket to somebody else.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams, fourteen shots better than his last visit to the Stadium and still detonating one hole per round
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A three-time Trophy winner produced a genuine personal best at PGA Catalunya - Stadium while conceding a quintuple bogey or worse in every single round.
discovered_storylines.shape: Williams opened by dropping eight shots in the first three holes at the Stadium, including an 8 at the par-three 5th (b35, and the R1 cold stretch), then found a 10 at the Tour's par-five 15th before steadying himself with a birdie late (b15). El Prat took an 8 off him at the 5th, answered by two clean holes at the 14th and 15th (b19, b47). The closing round contained an 11-shot haemorrhage from the 8th to the 11th with a 9 at the 10th inside it (b12, b03) — and, at the end of it, a 99 gross: his first sub-100 at the Stadium and fourteen shots better than TEG 6.
headline_candidates: Williams Breaks Hundred, Breaks Several Holes
One Explosion Per Round, Personal Best Anyway
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Gregg Williams gave up a quintuple bogey or worse in all four rounds, including eleven shots in four holes on the final day, and still walked off the Stadium course with the best gross figure he has ever posted there.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as supporting framing — Jon Baker's three Jacket runner-up finishes in the last four TEGs finally converted — but it rides behind the mandated close-finish frame, which the two brothers carried between them.

why_the_champion_won: Inherited, and he was the man in position to inherit: Jon Baker was best in the field in R1, never worse than 4th of 5 in any round, and posted a level 35 on the final day while Alex Baker, four clear after three holes, dropped seven shots at 4-6, eight at 12-14 and eight at 16-18 for 27 points — an ordinary round from Alex Baker would have won it.
